name: Customer Obsession
definition: Put the customer first, whether your work touches them directly or not. Foresee what customers expect and meet it before they ask.

rows.situation: When the problem is the customer's and not yours
rows.under: Optimizes for the internal roadmap and lets the customer wait.
rows.justRight: Starts from what the customer is trying to do, and works back to what you build.
rows.over: Chases every individual request until the product loses its shape.

rows.situation: When the customer has not asked yet
rows.under: Waits for the request. Builds only what arrived on a ticket.
rows.justRight: Sees what the customer will need next, and has it ready before they ask.
rows.over: Builds for imagined needs nobody has expressed, and ships features nobody uses.

rows.situation: When the customer has been let down
rows.under: Sends the templated apology and hopes it passes.
rows.justRight: Tells them what happened, what you are doing, and when. Then does it.
rows.over: Over-compensates every incident until the response costs more than the failure.

rows.situation: When the internal metric and the customer disagree
rows.under: Reports the metric and lets the experience rot.
rows.justRight: Treats the divergence as a broken metric, and goes to find out what the customer actually got.
rows.over: Refuses to use any metric, and runs the product on anecdote.

rows.situation: When two sides of the market want different things
rows.under: Serves whichever side is louder this quarter.
rows.justRight: Finds the answer that keeps both sides in the market, and says openly which side pays the cost.
rows.over: Waits for the option that costs neither side anything, and ships nothing.
